QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H fell from 0.520 (Nov 6) to 0.464 (Nov 19), below the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.925 measures fit only at supplied scales. Short/long H (0.413/0.580) show one line fits poorly across 8–63, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.755 suggests stronger volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell 0.010/0.015 over 1/5 observations. It’s 0.81 standard deviations below its prior-30 mean, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha rebounded from 3.198 (Nov 5) to 3.499 (Nov 19). Lower/higher means heavier/thinner fitted tails if the model fits. The 1,000-return window uses k=100, with x_min=0.02046 in absolute log-return units. Independent-return standard error is 0.350 and understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs yield 3.583/3.037, not a confidence interval. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SOXX.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:

Short/long H (0.368/0.549) show one straight line fits poorly across 8–63, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift.

H changed +0.0004/−0.0295 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 standardized deviation was −1.62, not a significance test because windows overlap. Absolute-return H=0.764 suggests stronger persistence in magnitudes, a volatility-clustering contrast, not tradable predictability.

These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
On Nov 19, SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.482, slightly below the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.948 measures fit only at supplied scales. Short/long slopes (0.409/0.568) show that one line fits poorly across 8–63, suggesting possible crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.689 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability. H fell 0.017/0.011 over one/five observations. Its prior-30 z-score was −0.61, not a significance test because windows overlap.

Hill alpha was 3.387 (1,000 returns, k=99, x_min=0.01460 absolute log-return units). Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The independent-return standard error (alpha/√k) is 0.340, understating uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs give 3.342/2.921, not confidence bounds.

H/alpha rose from 0.462/3.217 on Oct 9 to 0.527/3.401 on Nov 6 before easing. Unchanged top extremes can explain plateaus without implying a static market. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
